newsitem.title: INDIA: India soymeal prices ease on dull export demand.
newsitem.headline: India soymeal prices ease on dull export demand.

text.p: Indian soymeal prices eased during the week due to dull export and domestic demand and were expected to fall further, traders said on Tuesday.
They said soymeal for export was quoted at about $302 to $304 per tonne FAS compared with $321 to $323 per tonne last week.
"Soymeal prices may further decrease as export demand was poor," said an oilmeal broker in the central city of Indore, the hub of India's soybean industry.

Traders said Indian exporters have so far contracted to export about 2.2 million tonnes of soymeal in the 1996/97 (November-October) season. India exported about 2.6 million tonnes of soymeal in 1995/96.
Traders said soybean was currently quoted at 11,600 to 12,000 rupees per tonne in the domestic markets compared with about 11,900 to 12,400 rupees per tonne a week ago.

Indian rapeseed meal prices also eased during the week due to dull export demand, traders said. Rapeseed meal for export was currently quoted at $107 to $108 rupees per tonne compared with about $115 to $117 per tonne last week.
